name: Nexaline
manufacturer: Helix Biosystems (licensed); heavily counterfeited by the Gray Zone labs
description: A synthetic myelinogenic compound originally developed to accelerate BCI integration in new implant recipients. At therapeutic doses, Nexaline temporarily increases the signal density of neural-synthetic interface channels, effectively expanding BCI bandwidth by 200-400% for the duration. Users experience dramatically faster data throughput, simultaneous multi-channel processing, and a sensation described as 'thinking in parallel.' Helix markets the legitimate version to Tier 3-4 knowledge workers and tactical operators; counterfeit street versions have unpredictable potency.
effects: Simultaneous multi-channel data processing without cognitive bottleneck
Accelerated AR overlay rendering and interaction
Enhanced real-time tactical data integration for military augments
Sensation of expanded consciousness — 'thinking in widescreen'
Moderate euphoria from increased neural activity
side_effects: Information overload psychosis if BCI filters are not properly calibrated
Severe rebound bandwidth drop post-dose ('narrowing') lasting 6-12 hours
Counterfeit batches risk demyelination of neural interface tissue
Dissociation from physical body during peak — documented accidents from spatial unawareness
Long-term use degrades natural unaugmented cognition as brain offloads processing to BCI
cultural_context: Legitimate Nexaline is a productivity drug — analysts, architects, coders, and traders use it to hit deadline crunches or gain competitive edge in high-frequency markets. It's the 2200 equivalent of stimulant study drugs, normalized in Tier 3 professional culture. On the Gray Zone and in Tier 2, counterfeit Nexaline is a gamble people take for job interviews, gig work that requires BCI performance benchmarks, or simply to feel — briefly — like they have Tier 4 hardware. The counterfeit market is enormous and deadly. Helix doesn't crack down hard on counterfeiting because the existence of a street market normalizes the drug and drives aspirational legitimate sales.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 logistics worker took counterfeit Nexaline to pass a BCI performance test for a higher-paying position — now they're in a dissociative state, their BCI stuck in a feedback loop, unable to distinguish their AR overlay from physical reality. Someone needs to find the batch source before more people dose.

A Helix Biosystems researcher has discovered that long-term Nexaline use creates a specific, trackable pattern of BCI dependency — and that Helix's marketing division knows and has suppressed the data. The researcher is missing.

A tactical operator used prescription Nexaline during a mission and during the bandwidth peak, briefly intercepted and processed a data packet that was never meant for them — encrypted corporate traffic that someone very powerful wants back.
